stories.title: US memo: Megaspeed exec recruited to spy on Nvidia's CEO
stories.summary: A US intelligence memo reportedly says China's Ministry of State Security recruited a Megaspeed executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO, TechCrunch reports.
stories.more: TechCrunch reports that a memo circulated earlier this year claims China's Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive at Megaspeed to spy on Nvidia's chief executive. The report does not specify what information was obtained or how the alleged operation came to light. It adds to broader concerns about foreign efforts to access sensitive information from the US semiconductor industry.

stories.title: Anthropic presses ahead with pre-Thanksgiving IPO at lower valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic is proceeding with its IPO before Thanksgiving despite a tech selloff, accepting a valuation of $1.25-1.75 trillion, below its earlier $2 trillion target, The Decoder reports.
stories.more: The Decoder reports that Anthropic aims to raise $80 billion to $100 billion before Thanksgiving, pricing the offering at $1.25 trillion to $1.75 trillion rather than the previously hoped-for $2 trillion. The lower valuation comes amid a broader tech stock selloff. Rival OpenAI has also recently had to cut its own valuation, the report notes.

stories.title: Study: AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood false alarms
stories.summary: A study by Anthropic researcher Andy Hall finds AI models can spot problematic behavior in other AI agents' logs, but more exhaustive searches produce more false alarms, The Decoder reports.
stories.more: According to The Decoder, the study found that GPT-5 caught about 98 percent of reward-hacking cases when reviewing agent logs for misbehavior. However, the more exhaustively the search was tuned, the more false alarms piled up for human reviewers. The researchers conclude this isn't yet reliable enough for consistent safety checks on AI agents.

stories.title: Datasette stops sending 'link: rel=next' prefetch headers to Firefox
stories.summary: Simon Willison describes a Datasette fix (issue #3046) that stops sending 'link: rel="next"' HTTP headers to Firefox, which had been triggering unwanted prefetches of table pages.
stories.more: Willison writes that Firefox's network panel showed Datasette table pages triggering an HTTP prefetch of the next page of rows, caused by an HTTP 'link: rel="next"' header. He notes this is wasteful because only a small fraction of visitors to such pages click through to the next page, so prefetching wastes bandwidth. The fix, tracked as issue #3046, stops serving that header to Firefox for HTML pages.
